title: The Kite-Sail Grinder
markdown:
A few days before the Grand Gusty Fair, the Great Guzzle Grain Grinder stood as still as a statue. Its giant flat sails, which usually got shoved by the wind, drooped like wilted lettuce.

“Oh dear, oh dearie me,” sighed Oren the kite maker. His forehead went crinkly as a forgotten map. Twinkly eyes: not twinkly. “Without the grinder, no flour for Granny Buttercup’s famous flapjacks. No flapjacks at the fair is a party with no cake. Boring!”

Plum the rabbit hopped over, nose wiggling faster than a runaway jelly bean, and nudged Oren’s dusty boots.

“We have to help! Everyone’s counting on those flapjacks!”

They tiptoed to the giant. Oren gave a sail a mighty push. Nothing. Plum pushed with all his tiny might. Grunts. Slipping paws. Like shoving a giant sticky marshmallow. The sails did not wobble. Thump. They slumped, gloomy as a rainy Tuesday. The wind, usually a playful ear-tickler, was a whisper that could barely bother a ladybug.

“How can we ever get it moving?” Plum’s ears drooped.

Oren stared at the lifeless sails, then at his workshop: bright paper fluttering, long bendy sticks everywhere. His eyes lit like two brand-new fireflies.

“Wait a minute! What if we make the sails… like kites?”

Plum’s whiskers jumped. “Kites? I thought they just floated around looking pretty!”

“They catch the wind! They know how to dance with the breeze. Watch!” He dashed in, dashed out, bright blue kite paper and a long light stick. He held it up. Wind caught it. He tilted. A gentle curve. “The wind wants to push it up and away. But if we want a sideways shove—” he scooped the paper like a little spoon “—this shape makes the wind push sideways, with all its might. A big friendly shove!”

Plum’s pink nose twitched furiously. Curved paper grabbed more air. More oomph. “A little wind-trap! It holds onto the breeze and says, you’re not getting away from me!”

They spent the afternoon on shapes: flat, bumpy, wonderfully curved. Held them up. Breeze tugging ears. Curved ones always caught the most. They wanted to leap out of paws and fly. Flat ones fluttered and sighed, which is paper for I give up.

“This is it!” Oren gathered strong paper, sticky glue, extra-long bendy sticks. “New blades. Shaped like the best kite wings. Blades that love to dance with the wind!”

A flurry of cutting, pasting, sticking, tying. Oren’s fingers a blur. Plum’s paws holding steady. Four big curved sails, colourful as a rainbow after a summer shower, went onto the grinder in place of the old flat sad ones.

A lovely playful breeze rustled the trees.

“Here it comes!” Plum’s heart did a drum solo.

The breeze met the new sails. Instead of bouncing off, it hugged them and pushed. The giant sails turned — slowly, then faster. Colourful curves singing. The Great Guzzle Grain Grinder roared to life, a cheerful hum.

“YESSS!” Shoulders lighter than feathers.

Friends who had been sighing about flapjacks came running. Granny Buttercup peered from her cottage, eyes wide. Gran Maple, the wise old badger, smiled her warmest.

“Clever you two. You’ve figured out a way to catch the wind. It’s all about the shape. This curved shape is called an airfoil. It makes the wind push harder!”

Oren wiped glue from his nose. “So our kite-sails are like tiny aeroplane wings for the grain grinder?”

“Exactly.” Gran Maple chuckled. “The wind can be a powerful helper if you know how to shape things nicely.”

She did not wink about boats and trick-kites as a homework list. Oren and Plum already had heads full of whizzy breezy ideas, and Granny Buttercup had already heated the pan. The grinder kept turning. Flour would follow. Flapjacks, if the wind held, would too.
characters: Oren (kite maker), Plum (rabbit), Gran Maple (badger), Granny Buttercup (flapjack baker)
author: StoryGen Community
